text:
Sofia: Quick sync — AtlasPay wants a drop-in replacement for CompetitorX for their payments chat assistant. Key asks: identical response shape, prompt parity, and a direct cost comparison. They also sent a security questionnaire.

Ravi: Cool. Plan idea: 1) compat shim that maps CompetitorX request/response fields to our API, 2) prompt mapping doc + canonical prompt set for parity tests, 3) pricing worksheet comparing hosted per-token vs Dedicated commit for their volume.

Liam: For the compat shim, two engineering edges: streaming behavior and metadata headers. Their client assumes single final payload (no chunking). We can add a "single-chunk" mode to the runtime to satisfy them for the POC.

Nina: Security note — AtlasPay requires SOC2+ and an internal vulnerability disclosure policy. Procurement also asked about customer-managed KMS and IP allowlisting for the POC. I put the questionnaire into Legal.

Ravi: @Liam can you give a quick dev estimate for: shim + single-chunk mode + basic field mappings? Also need rough perf impact so we can set expectations.

Liam: Estimate: shim + mapping middleware ~2 dev-days, single-chunk toggle ~1 dev-day, testing + infra ~1 day. Perf: expect ~5-10% CPU increase and tail latency +20-50ms depending on sequence length.

Sofia: AtlasPay also asked about billing parity: they want a sample bill for 1M tokens/month + cost under a 3-month Dedicated commit. Can we get a conservative delta vs CompetitorX?

Ravi: I'll draft a simple calc. For the SOW, suggest offering a temporary credit/discount during the POC to offset integration risk. Also propose a canary routing plan: 10% of traffic to start, expand as parity tests pass.

Nina: On data handling: they asked if we persist prompts for analytics. Answer: by default we retain metrics but can enable stricter retention or no logging for the POC. Need ops sign-off for the no-logging mode.

deploy-bot: branch created: atlaspay-compat-poc-323000 (CI green).

Sofia: Great. Next steps: Ravi to share pricing worksheet + parity test plan by EOD tomorrow. Liam to prototype single-chunk toggle and a mapping example. Nina to surface legal/security blockers from questionnaire. I'll schedule tech deep-dive with AtlasPay Fri 10am PT.

Ravi: I'll assemble a 30-minute demo script focusing on prompt parity tests (50 seed prompts) and a runbook for divergence handling — fallback to CompetitorX endpoint for specific prompts if needed.

Liam: Quick sample mapping snippet to illustrate field renames for the shim:
```
# request mapping example
{
  "user_input": payload.prompt,
  "conversation_id": payload.session_id
}

# response mapping example
{
  "text": resp.output_text,
  "tokens": resp.token_count
}
```

Sofia: Perfect — that will help procurement visualize the integration. I'll cc Legal on the SOW draft. :thumbsup:

Ravi: Also flagging one enterprise blocker: AtlasPay wants a 99.99% uptime SLA for production. Need PM/Infra to confirm if Dedicated can be SLA-backed within their region.

Liam: Noted. For the POC we can do soft SLA via dedicated pool but will need account team + infra to lock eventual contract terms.

Sofia: Thanks team — I'll send the calendar invite and share this thread with AtlasPay as meeting prep.
